# triage

GitHub issues into TODO.md through a program, with a Read-only proposer's bounded summary and labels, and the pre-commit link guard.

- Spec: `docs/features/triage/spec.md`
- Contract: `docs/features/triage/contract.md`

## Files

```
go: tools/triage/**
go: internal/triage/**
```

## Decisions

- `kb:adr/issue-daemon-creates-issues-only` — The daemon's involvement ends at creating an issue: no reading, labels or status sync; a filed issue's fate is a developer-workflow concern outside musterd. (accepted, 2026-08-31; features: issue, triage) → `docs/adr/issue-daemon-creates-issues-only.md`
- `kb:adr/process-land-skill-is-the-landing-ritual` — Landing is its own step: it gates on an approved review, composes the closing subject, shows the predicted bump, pushes, and deletes the branch by content diff. (accepted, 2026-08-31; features: release, triage) → `docs/adr/process-land-skill-is-the-landing-ritual.md`
- `kb:adr/triage-bounded-proposer-summary-reaches-the-backlog` — The Read-only proposer's two bounded, ASCII, link-free, tripwire-checked sentences reach TODO.md; a program still owns everything from fetch to commit. (accepted, 2026-10-15; features: triage) → `docs/adr/triage-bounded-proposer-summary-reaches-the-backlog.md`
- `kb:adr/triage-every-entry-carries-the-header-safe-title` — One entry template on every route: HeaderSafe title, summary, quoted error, a fact line from validated snapshot leaves, labels; the header stays on one line. (accepted, 2026-10-15; features: triage) → `docs/adr/triage-every-entry-carries-the-header-safe-title.md`
- `kb:adr/triage-issue-closes-when-fix-lands` — An issue closes when the fix lands on main via a closes reference in the squash subject, never at triage; duplicates and invalid issues close with approval. (accepted, 2026-08-31; features: triage, release) → `docs/adr/triage-issue-closes-when-fix-lands.md`
- `kb:adr/triage-labels-from-validated-names` — apply labels each filed issue through gh with names from closed lists a test holds to conventions § Issue labels; the comment stays a manual gh call. (accepted, 2026-10-15; features: triage) → `docs/adr/triage-labels-from-validated-names.md`
- `kb:adr/triage-owner-issues-normal-unless-held` — An OWNER-filed issue takes the normal path unless a danger signal fires — counts never demote it — and is then readable in the session; MEMBER earns nothing (accepted, 2026-10-15; features: triage) → `docs/adr/triage-owner-issues-normal-unless-held.md`
- `kb:adr/triage-routing-by-signals-not-counts` — An issue routes on danger signals — bidi, a rule-family hit, zero-width text, a classifier score — never on sanitiser counts, which are reported only. (accepted, 2026-10-15; features: triage) → `docs/adr/triage-routing-by-signals-not-counts.md`
- `kb:adr/triage-section-defaults-to-issues` — Every new entry files under the Issues section unless --section or a decisions override says otherwise; the run never asks, and ranking is a hand edit after. (accepted, 2026-10-15; features: triage) → `docs/adr/triage-section-defaults-to-issues.md`
- `kb:adr/triage-snapshot-untrusted-drop-and-count` — The issue's snapshot JSON is untrusted like the body; a union schema of every shape ever emitted drops and counts unknown fields; the table says reported. (accepted, 2026-09-11; features: triage, issue) → `docs/adr/triage-snapshot-untrusted-drop-and-count.md`
- `kb:adr/triage-state-derived-from-todo` — Triage state is derived, not stored: an issue is triaged iff its number appears in the backlog file; no labels, no close state, no second list to keep in sync. (accepted, 2026-08-31; features: triage) → `docs/adr/triage-state-derived-from-todo.md`

## Retired, rejected and superseded

- `kb:adr/triage-auto-close-never` — A tripwire hit holds an issue for the developer; triage never closes one automatically, since that is an outward write driven by attacker input. (rejected, 2026-09-11; features: triage) → `docs/adr/triage-auto-close-never.md`
- `kb:adr/triage-normal-path-carries-the-sanitised-title` — A trusted, unflagged issue renders with the sanitised title; it is the second attacker-derived field in the backlog and HeaderSafe is its guard. (superseded, 2026-09-21; features: triage) → `docs/adr/triage-normal-path-carries-the-sanitised-title.md`
- `kb:adr/triage-owner-filed-artifacts-readable-in-session` — The session may read an OWNER-filed, unflagged issue's sanitised artifact — never the raw ticket, and OWNER rather than the wider trusted set. (superseded, 2026-09-21; features: triage) → `docs/adr/triage-owner-filed-artifacts-readable-in-session.md`
- `kb:adr/triage-program-not-model-between-github-and-todo` — Nothing between GitHub and the backlog diff is a model with tools: a program fetches, sanitises, routes, splices and commits; a Read-only subagent summarises. (superseded, 2026-09-11; features: triage) → `docs/adr/triage-program-not-model-between-github-and-todo.md`
- `kb:adr/triage-sandboxing-rejected-for-read-only-proposer` — Sandboxing the issue-reading step is not used; capability removal beats isolation for a read-only job, and the platform sandbox has no hard network boundary. (rejected, 2026-09-11; features: triage) → `docs/adr/triage-sandboxing-rejected-for-read-only-proposer.md`
